                    ### Question
                    A 33-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of progressive hair loss from his scalp. He first noticed receding of the hairline over the bitemporal regions of his scalp 5 years ago. Since then, his hair has gradually become thinner over the crown of his head. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. Examination shows diffuse, nonscarring hair loss over the scalp with a bitemporal pattern of recession. Administration of which of the following drugs is most appropriate to treat this patient's hair loss?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Flutamide
opb. Clomipramine
opc. Triamcinolone
opd. Levothyroxine
ope. Finasteride

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Male pattern baldness, also known as androgenetic alopecia, is characterized by hair follicle miniaturization due to increased levels of dihydrotestosterone (DHT) binding to androgen receptors. This leads to shortening of the anagen phase of the hair growth cycle and progressive hair loss. The most appropriate treatment for this condition is the administration of Finasteride, which inhibits the conversion of testosterone to DHT. Evidence supports the role of Finasteride in treating alopecia by targeting the underlying hormonal mechanism.
